card: Automatically deletes the obsolete legacy coinstats index directory at indexes/coinstats on startup when -coinstatsindex is enabled. An incompatible format change in v30 moved active data to indexes/coinstatsindex while preserving the old directory so users could downgrade to v29 without resyncing. With v29 reaching end-of-life, this change fulfills an existing TODO in the codebase to clean up obsolete database files and reclaim disk space.
changed_since_previous: Added a release note documenting the automatic directory deletion in doc/release-notes-coinstatsindex-cleanup.md.
evidence: A code comment and TODO introduced during the v30 format change in #30469 scheduled deletion: 'Change this to deleting the old index with v31.'
Author notes in the description that with v32 branched off and v29 reaching EOL, the scheduled cleanup should proceed for v33.
problem: Nodes upgraded from v29 or earlier retain the superseded `indexes/coinstats` index directory on disk indefinitely, needlessly consuming disk space unless manually deleted.

risk.why: A flaw in filesystem path construction or deletion logic could delete unexpected files, though the target directory path is hardcoded to the legacy index location.

summary: Deletes the obsolete `indexes/coinstats` database directory automatically on startup when `CoinStatsIndex` is initialized. It calls `DestroyDB` on the old LevelDB path and removes the legacy folder, logging an informational message on success or a warning if removal fails.
